diagnosis.root_cause: Customer ONU 22371 is currently offline and deregistered from MPCP (Unauth/MPCP DEREG), with no live optical readings. The historical optical, bias-current, distance, power-supply, and temperature readings were stable and healthy, so there is no evidence of fibre, laser, PON-port, splitter, OLT, VLAN, router, or RADIUS failure. The most likely cause is a customer-side ONU power or local-fibre/CPE issue.
evidence: The subscriber ONU status is offline, and the live probe confirms online=0, auth_flag=Unauth, and exchange=MPCP DEREG.
The zero/null RX and TX values are correctly interpreted as no reading because the ONU is offline, not as strong optical signal.
Seven days of historical RX power stayed around -22.3 to -23.1 dBm, which is normal and within the healthy noise range; TX power stayed around +2.3 dBm, also normal.
TX bias current remained approximately 10.8-11.7 mA, with no rising-bias pattern indicating laser ageing.
Distance remained constant at 294 m, so there is no evidence of a fibre-path change.
The OLT is reachable and healthy: all eight PONs passed, CPU and memory are normal, temperature is normal, and uptime is stable.
Other ONUs on EPON0/6 are online with normal optical levels, ruling out a PON-port failure or broad splitter failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy, the expected customer VLAN 1016 is present, and RADIUS data is consistent with CRM, ruling out router, VLAN, and authentication/configuration faults.
The customer's session count and duration are normal, with no session-flapping or authentication pattern.

The OLT has 25 offline of 298 customers, versus an expected background level of about 14; this is elevated but not sufficient to establish an OLT-wide outage, and the subscriber-specific evidence remains an ONU offline condition.

remediation.action: Treat the customer ONU as offline rather than as an OLT or PON outage. Contact the customer or dispatch support to verify ONU power, LEDs, power adapter, and the indoor/drop fibre connection; power-cycle or replace the ONU if necessary, then verify MPCP registration and optical readings. Do not change RADIUS, VLAN, OLT, or router configuration. Monitor the other offline ONUs separately; the OLT-wide offline count is within plausible background range and the PON port remains operational.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
